tooltip.recompile.animal_bait: Place on grass and step away - wildlife will not come while you are near. Keep baits apart.
jade.recompile.compost_empty: Empty - feed it muck or fiber
jade.recompile.workbench_empty: Rack a Scrap Knife or Prybar
jade.recompile.workbench_ready: Hold right-click to break it down
jei.recompile.info.compost_heap: A 2x2x2 salvage cage that composts the dump's organics into Fertilizer. Place the core and build the cage from seven Machine Frames. Feed it any compostable - Organic Muck, Fiber Scrap, or plant matter like leaves, saplings, grass, crops and seeds: every few forms a layer, each layer ripens on its own, and a finished layer is right-clicked out for one Fertilizer. It never has to be full.
jei.recompile.info.fertilizer: Finished compost from the Compost Heap. Right-click reclaimed grass to scatter weeds and wildflowers across it - rung 2 of bringing the world back - or right-click mycelium to grow mushrooms. It does nothing on the raw dump, so heal the ground with a Grass Spreader first. The plants it grows are torn out by the encroaching dump before it takes the grass, so a fertilized border holds a little longer.
jei.recompile.info.grass_spreader: Waters the ground around it, turning coarse dirt and dirt to grass one block at a time. Build up from the core: Water Tank, Pump, Solar Panel on top, and a Copper Pipe on each side of the Pump. It sits idle until the whole tower is up.
jei.recompile.info.rain_collector: Rain is the only source of fresh water in this world. Put a Rain Collector Funnel on top and leave it under open sky. Take water out with a bucket or a glass bottle.

book.recompile.guide.name: The Salvager's Manual
book.recompile.guide.tooltip: A field guide to a world made of garbage.
book.recompile.guide.getting_started.the:
This is a world built from garbage. There are no ores, no trees, no animals, and no caves worth the trip. The surface is coarse dirt from edge to edge, and everything you need is buried in the mounds of trash on top of it.

Materials do not come from mining. They come from picking through garbage. The early game is learning how.

The one thing you must get right at the start: when you create the world, open the More tab and set the World Type to Garbage World. A normal world ignores the preset and drops you in vanilla terrain, which is the most common reason people think the mod is not working.

The garbage biome has no mob spawns by design. Nothing hunts you here, and nothing gives you meat.
book.recompile.guide.getting_started.pic:
Dig a Block of Garbage and it drops itself, like gravel (it also falls like gravel, so mind what is above you). The value is inside: place it back down and right-click it with an empty hand to pull one item out. Right-click again for the next.

Each block only has so much in it. After a handful of pulls it crumbles and is gone. What you get is random, weighted toward common scrap.

Trash Bags and Compacted Bales are richer streams than a plain garbage block, with their own drop tables. Some pulls want a tool in hand rather than a bare hand. If a block will not give anything up, check what it expects (Jade shows the hint).
book.recompile.guide.getting_started.mat:
Nine base materials carry the whole early game:

Junk - the filler; the bulk sink and a crafting stand-in.
Scrap Metal - the metal vocabulary.
Rebar - structural; a crafting spine.
Plastic Scrap - plastics and panels.
Glass Shards - glass and cullet.
Fiber Scrap - cloth and padding.
Organic Muck - compost feed.
E-Scrap - the rare electronic bits.
Tin Can - food (see Survival & Shelter).

You will read these names on every recipe. JEI shows which block or tool each one feeds.
book.recompile.guide.getting_started.sea: The Nether and the End are sealed. Portals will not form. Those doors open in a later version, when each themed dimension is ready; until then the trash economy stays closed, so vanilla dimensions cannot leak free resources into it.
book.recompile.guide.tools.salvage.name: Salvage Tools
book.recompile.guide.tools.salvage.intro:
The tools here are not the wood-to-stone-to-iron ladder. They are salvage tools, crafted from the base materials, and each opens something specific:

Prybar - pries open Bulky Waste.
Scrap Knife - cuts open Tin Cans and cuts down a Mattress at the workbench.
Junk Shovel - digs the garbage world's coarse dirt and mounds faster.

The right tool is often the difference between a block giving something up and giving nothing.
book.recompile.guide.tools.bulky.name: Bulky Waste
book.recompile.guide.tools.bulky.intro.t:
Bulky Waste is the big buried item, not a pick-through block. Right-click it with a Prybar and it opens in one action: it drops a single find and breaks. Without a Prybar it tells you what it needs, and mining it by hand gives nothing.

Finds are how you get things you cannot pull from loose garbage, including the parts that build machines. A mattress becomes a bed; an appliance gives up a Pump. Nothing enters this world without a way to break it back down.
book.recompile.guide.workstations.crafti:
There is no wood, so there is no vanilla crafting table. You craft at the Scrap Crafting Table, and it is one of the first things you build.

It does one thing the vanilla table cannot: it reaches into the Scrap Network. Stand it against your Scrap Bins and Barrel and it crafts straight from what they hold, so you do not have to pull materials into the grid by hand first.
book.recompile.guide.workstations.sortin:
The Tarp sifts garbage without picking through it by hand. Right-click it holding a stack of garbage, trash bags, bales, or Stone Rubble and it sifts the drops straight onto the ground around it.

It has no screen and stores nothing. It is a faster hand, not a machine, so stand over a place you do not mind covering in loose items, or feed it next to a Scrap Barrel.
book.recompile.guide.workstations.workbe:
The Workbench tears salvage back into materials. Rack a Scrap Knife or a Prybar on it first (right-click with the tool), then hold right-click on the workbench with an item to break it down. The racked tool takes durability as it works; a broken tool stops the line.

Jade shows the racked tool, its durability, and whether what you are holding has any salvage value.
book.recompile.guide.workstations.scrap_: Every vanilla container needs wood, and there is none, so storage is its own tier. The Scrap Barrel is the general one: it opens the normal chest screen and holds a chest's worth of anything.

A Scrap Bin binds to a single item type. The first thing you file into an empty bin sets it, and after that the bin only takes that item.

Line up a wall of bins to sort one material each, then let the Scrap Network keep them filled.
book.recompile.guide.workstations.burn_b: A furnace you feed by hand

The Burn Barrel is the world's smelter. It opens the normal furnace screen, so smelting works the way you expect, with one difference: it takes no automation. Hoppers and pipes cannot push into or pull out of it. You load and unload it by hand.

It burns Oily Rag and the other salvage fuels. It lights up while it is running.
book.recompile.guide.workstations.scrap_:
Place the station blocks touching, sharing a face, and they form one cluster: the Scrap Crafting Table, Scrap Bins, the Scrap Barrel, the Sorting Tarp, the Workbench, and the Burn Barrel.

When you file items in, they route through the cluster on their own. A bound bin that matches takes the item first, then an empty bin, then the Barrel. No pipes, no hoppers, no screen; just put the blocks next to each other.
Blocks that route to each other
book.recompile.guide.survival.food.name: Feeding Yourself
book.recompile.guide.survival.food.intro:
The garbage biome spawns nothing, so hunting is not on the menu. Food comes from two places.

Tin Cans turn up in the pull streams. You cannot eat a sealed can; cut it open with a Scrap Knife first, then eat what is inside.

Dump Mushrooms grow on mycelium in the dump. Forage them, and replant them like vanilla mushrooms to keep a renewable patch.
book.recompile.guide.survival.food.mushr: A Dump Mushroom is a placeable item. Put it back down on mycelium and it grows again, so a foraged patch is a food source you can farm rather than strip. Fertilizer on mycelium (see Reclamation) grows more.
book.recompile.guide.survival.lighting.i:
No coal on the surface and no sticks means no vanilla torch on the normal path. Light comes from the Scrap Torch, made with an Oily Rag as the fuel.

One torch item places on the floor or on a wall, whichever surface you click.
book.recompile.guide.survival.water.name: The Rain Collector
book.recompile.guide.survival.water.intr:
There are no rivers or springs, so rain is the only fresh water. The Rain Collector catches it.

Place the collector, put a Rain Collector Funnel (a Machine Frame wrapped in Plastic Scrap) on top of it, and leave it under open sky; it fills when it rains. Draw water out with a bucket or a glass bottle. If you break the collector, the water it is holding comes with it and is there again when you replace it.
book.recompile.guide.survival.building.i:
Once you are drowning in scrap, the building blocks are the sink. Each material family presses into a full block plus a slab, stairs, and wall (glass adds a pane):

Pressed Junk - the everyday grey block.
Scrap Plating - metal.
Corrugated Metal - ribbed metal.
Plastic Panel - plastics.
Cullet Glass - remelted glass shards, with a pane.

These are craft targets, not drops. They turn a materials surplus into a base.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.machine:
The reclamation machines are multiblocks: a core block plus a set of parts stacked around it in a fixed shape. There are two ways to build one.

Place the core with all the parts in your inventory and it assembles itself, consuming the parts. A grey and red preview shows the footprint before you commit, so you can see if it fits. Or place the core and stack the parts by hand in the right spots.

A machine only works once it is fully formed. Break any block of it and the whole thing comes apart, dropping its parts.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.encroac:
Bringing the world back is not a one-time act. The dump takes green ground back.

Grass on the border of healed and unhealed ground reverts to coarse dirt over time. Plants you scatter are torn out first, before the grass under them, so a planted edge buys the grass a little longer. Logs and leaves make ground permanent.

Only the green is contested; it never eats down to bare rock. The sweep only runs near players, so a base does not rot while you are away.
Reclaimed ground rots at the edges

Farmland is defended by water, not by grass. A watered plot holds against the dump. A plot that dries out is taken back with the soil under it. A crop on lost farmland pops off as an item, so you lose the plot and the growth but keep the seed. Keep your fields irrigated.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.grass_s:
Rung one of reclamation. The Grass Spreader waters the ground around it and turns coarse dirt straight to grass, one block at a time. It also keeps nearby farmland wet, like a water source.

Build it up from the core: a Water Tank on the core, a Pump above that, a Solar Panel on top, and a Copper Pipe on each of the four sides of the Pump. It sits idle until the whole tower is up, and needs water in the tank to run.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.vegetat:
Rung two. Right-click reclaimed grass with Fertilizer to scatter weeds and wildflowers across it - the pioneer plants that come back to disturbed ground.

Fertilizer does nothing on the raw dump, so heal the ground with a Grass Spreader first. The plants it grows are the first thing the dump strips at a contested edge, so a fertilized border holds a little longer while you push out.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.farming:
Rung three. A hoe will not till the dump. You craft farmland instead: Fertilizer plus dirt (or coarse dirt and more fertilizer). The compost recipe is the only way to a plot.

Seeds are not bought or found loose; they come from compost. The Heap now and then drops an Unknown Seedling that becomes a random one of the six crops when you plant it.

Keep plots watered with a Grass Spreader or rain. A dry plot dries out and the dump takes it.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.compost:
Fertilizer comes from the Compost Heap, a two-by-two-by-two salvage cage: place the core and build the cage from seven Machine Frames (it assembles itself if you carry them).

Feed it any compostable - Organic Muck, Fiber Scrap, or plant matter like leaves, grass, saplings, crops and seeds. Every few items form a layer, each layer ripens on its own timer, and a ripe layer is right-clicked out for one Fertilizer. It never has to be full to give something back.
book.recompile.guide.reclamation.sapling:
Saplings are stripped from every drop, so you will never have one in your inventory. This is on purpose. A found sapling could grow a tree on raw coarse dirt and permanently anchor ground you have not actually reclaimed.

Trees come from a machine planter (a later tier), which is the only thing that places a sapling. Until then, reclamation tops out at grass, plants, and crops.
book.recompile.guide.collectibles.puzzle:
The Puzzle Cube is the first collectible, and the only one you assemble. Its nine pieces turn up rarely in the pull streams; when you have all nine, fill the crafting grid with them to build the cube.

The cube is a real block you place and display. Craft it with itself to scramble it, and again to solve it.
book.recompile.guide.collectibles.curios:
Some curios are found whole rather than assembled - an avocado, a wrapped present, a gold coin, a toy car. They are rare, a few times rarer than a single Puzzle Cube piece, and they turn up intact in the same pick-through streams.

There is nothing to craft; you either find one or you do not. Set it on a pedestal and keep looking for the rest.
book.recompile.guide.collectibles.pedest:
The Display Pedestal holds one item and floats it, slowly turning, above the cap. It takes any item, so a collectible is only the obvious thing to set on it. It is a display, not storage: no hopper feeds it, and it drops what it holds when you take it or break it.

Because it shows the item's real model, a placed block like the Puzzle Cube stands up there as a true 3D object.
book.recompile.guide.reference.toggles.i:
Most of the mod's behavior is config-gated. Defaults are the intended game, but a pack or a player can change them.

The switches worth knowing: garbage-block gravity, the encroachment sweep, the dimension lockout, and the reclamation numbers. This entry is the orientation; the config file itself is where the values live and is commented per option.
book.recompile.guide.reference.viewers.i:
Two viewer mods, if you run them, surface the non-vanilla mechanics in-game.

JEI adds Sorting, Cutting, and Prying categories, so you can look up what a garbage block, a knife, or a prybar yields, and it shows the Scrap Crafting Table as the station.

Jade shows block hints on look: which tool a block wants, how far a Grass Spreader reaches, how many layers a Compost Heap has, and the sort progress on a garbage block.
The mechanics that are not recipes
message.recompile.torch_no_fuel: The torch is empty - right-click with an Oily Rag to charge it
message.recompile.torch_needs_rag: You need an Oily Rag to charge the torch
tooltip.recompile.torch_charge_hint: Right-click with an Oily Rag to charge
message.recompile.torch_too_full: The torch is too full to take a whole rag
jei.recompile.info.burn_barrel: Burns refuse only: food, and scrap metal for copper. It will not smelt ore, sand, stone or logs - a drum fire does not get hot enough. Upgrade it into a Cupola Furnace to smelt everything else.
jei.recompile.info.cupola_furnace: A coke-fired shaft furnace for remelting scrap. Smelts everything the Burn Barrel does and everything it refuses, including steel offcuts into iron. Unlike the barrel it takes hoppers.
jei.recompile.info.cutting_torch: Right-click holding the torch to feed it an Oily Rag. Each rag is worth 8 cuts and it holds 64. Cutting steel spends one charge; with an empty torch the cut is refused.
jei.recompile.info.steel_offcut: Cut off a Steel I-Beam with a Cutting Torch. Remelt it into iron in a Cupola Furnace - the Burn Barrel will not take it.
jei.recompile.info.burner_generator: Burns refuse for power. Right-click it holding any furnace fuel - an Oily Rag will do - and it runs until that fuel is spent, feeding energy to whatever it is touching. It takes one fuel at a time and refuses a second while lit, so nothing is wasted. No screen: what you see on top is whether it is burning.
